boards.title: Your First Weekend at Pitzer College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, on-campus first-weekend sequence: get oriented, eat, explore Pitzer’s outdoor spaces, make something, and finish with art.

cards.title: Start at Avery Gate
cards.subtitle: Arrival point on the Pitzer campus map
cards.notes: Use this named campus landmark as a starting point, then pull up the interactive map before walking toward the central academic area.
cards.short_summary: Begin by getting your bearings at a named campus entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer’s current campus map identifies Avery Gate as location 32.
cards.access_notes: Use the college’s interactive campus map for wayfinding.

cards.title: Settle in on The Mounds
cards.subtitle: Pellissier Mall, Pitzer campus
cards.notes: Bring a book, sketchpad, or new hallmate for a daytime pause on this central lawn before continuing across campus.
cards.short_summary: Take a relaxed outdoor break in Pitzer’s central green space.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer’s walking tour describes The Mounds as a grass section running from Brant Clock Tower to McConnell Center and a site for orientation and campus events.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; check the campus calendar if an event is scheduled.

cards.title: Have a meal at McConnell Bistro
cards.subtitle: McConnell Center dining hall
cards.notes: Check the day’s menu, then use a meal-plan option or another eligible payment method for a first shared campus meal.
cards.short_summary: Eat together at Pitzer’s seven-day dining hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer states that McConnell Bistro serves made-from-scratch meals seven days a week and offers several food stations.
cards.access_notes: Dining requires an applicable meal plan or payment; consult the current menu for service details.

cards.title: Pick up something at Shakedown Café
cards.subtitle: Pitzer campus café
cards.notes: Make this a casual stop for a snack or drink, and check the café’s current serving information before heading over.
cards.short_summary: Add a café stop centered on seasonal, locally sourced food.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer says the student-started Shakedown Café focuses on sustainable, seasonal, and locally sourced goods.
cards.access_notes: Food and drinks require purchase or applicable dining funds; verify current offerings before visiting.

cards.title: Walk the Mead Hall murals
cards.subtitle: Mead Hall exterior and hallways
cards.notes: Take a slow lap to look at the student-made murals, then photograph only what is appropriate in an active residence hall.
cards.short_summary: See a long-running, student-created layer of Pitzer’s campus art.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer describes Mead Hall as historically known for student murals on its exterior walls and hallways spanning decades.
cards.access_notes: Mead Hall is a residence hall; respect residents and posted access guidance.

cards.title: Check what’s happening at Grove House
cards.subtitle: Performance and meeting space on campus
cards.notes: Look for an open mic, reading, art opening, or Groove at the Grove listing, then attend only the event’s posted public or student access.
cards.short_summary: Use a named arts venue to find a low-pressure community event.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer says Grove House hosts open mics, readings, art openings, and Groove at the Grove music performances.
cards.access_notes: Programming varies; confirm event time and eligibility on Pitzer’s calendar.

cards.title: Take the Outback trail
cards.subtitle: Northeast Pitzer campus, north of East and West Halls
cards.notes: Enter from north of East and West Halls, stay on the trail, and pack out anything you bring to help protect the restoration area.
cards.short_summary: Walk through Pitzer’s rare alluvial sage scrub preserve.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer identifies the Outback Preserve as over three acres of alluvial sage scrub and directs visitors to stay on the trail.
cards.access_notes: Stay on designated trails; follow the preserve’s no-smoking and pack-out guidance.

cards.entity_name: Gold Student Health and Wellness Center
cards.title: Move at the Gold Student Center
cards.subtitle: GSC, near Pitzer’s first-year residence halls
cards.notes: Use the gym, pool, or Pilates and yoga studios according to the facility’s current student access rules and class schedule.
cards.short_summary: Build in a recreation stop close to the first-year halls.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer identifies the Gold Student Health and Wellness Center as an on-campus recreation home with a gym, pool, and Pilates and yoga studios.
cards.access_notes: Facility and class access are subject to current student policies and schedules.

cards.title: See what’s on at Nichols Gallery
cards.subtitle: Broad Center, 1060 N. Mills Ave.
cards.notes: Visit during the posted Wednesday–Saturday afternoon hours, or contact the gallery in advance if you need to arrange another time.
cards.short_summary: End with a free contemporary-art stop in the Broad Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer states that Nichols Gallery is in the Broad Center, exhibitions are always free, and regular hours are Wednesday–Saturday, 1–4 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Regular hours: Wednesday–Saturday, 1–4 p.m.; exhibitions may be viewed outside those hours by appointment.

cards.title: Continue to Lenzner Gallery
cards.subtitle: Atherton Hall, 1150 Pitzer Service Rd.
cards.notes: Pair this gallery with Nichols if both are open, and use the accessible path or drop-off information if that makes the visit easier.
cards.short_summary: Complete the art walk at Pitzer’s second free exhibition space.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer lists the Lenzner Family Art Gallery in Atherton Hall and says its exhibitions are always free.
cards.access_notes: Regular hours: Wednesday–Saturday, 1–4 p.m.; both galleries are wheelchair accessible.
